instruction: Student question regarding Science (Class 9): Why do noble gases like Helium and Neon have zero valency?
output: Helium has 2 valence electrons filling its K-shell (duplet), and Neon has 8 valence electrons filling its L-shell (octet). Since their outer energy shells are completely full, they do not gain, lose, or share electrons, so their combining capacity (valency) is zero.

instruction: Student question regarding Science (Class 10): Why does the blue color of copper sulfate solution fade when an iron nail is immersed in it?
output: Iron is more reactive than copper and displaces copper from copper sulfate solution forming light green ferrous sulfate (FeSO4) and depositing brown copper.
